Six weeks to all eight videos in two cuts each, then a steady three posts a week with no further shooting. Posting starts in week 1 with the posts that need no video, so the account is never silent while the filming happens.
WHAT FIXES THE ORDER — READ BEFORE YOU PLAN A DATE

Three things decide the sequence, and none of them is preference. V4 can only be filmed on a MONDAY, because the vouchers it shows are built by the Sunday 02:00 job — miss the Monday and it waits a week. V6 needs a real venue at night with its pin already set, so it is tied to a venue visit rather than a desk day. V8 is assembled from footage the other seven produce, so it cannot come first however much you want it to.
THE THREE SHOOTS — PLAN THESE AS EVENTS, NOT TASKS
One evening at your own desk, plus ten minutes on the pavement outside for V6. No venue, no permission, no night shoot.

TWO CUTS FROM EVERY RECORDING — WHY THE LONG ONE EXISTS

Eight to twenty seconds shows a feature; it cannot explain a product nobody has heard of. The answer is not to slow the short one down but to take two cuts from the same footage — record once, cut twice.

values: Make the Videos — tools, cost, and the eight scripts
Which generator to use and what it costs, how to record the real screens for free, the shoot plan, the consent rules, and the eight three-part prompts.
THE ONE IDEA TO SELL, BEFORE ANY SINGLE FEATURE

Nobody else in KL nightlife closes the loop. The competitor is not another app — it is a WhatsApp group, an Excel file and a paper chit. Rival tools each do one piece. InnocenZ is the only one where a single action flows all the way through:
A PR taps check-in at the door
It becomes a pay line for that day
The weekly voucher takes her signature
The venue sees who sold what
Say this once a month in one 20-second video (V8 on the Make the Videos tab) and let every other post be a single link in that chain. It is the claim a spreadsheet cannot answer.
HOW A VIDEO GETS MADE — THREE STEPS, NONE OF THEM AT A VENUE

⚠ NO VENUE VISITS. Nothing in this set needs a nightclub, a night shoot or anybody’s permission. The openers are generated from the prompts on this tab, the screens are recorded at your own desk, and V6 — the one that used to need a venue — is walked outside your own door once the demo pin is moved to your building.

Open the video’s OPENING SHOT row on this tab. Copy the cell whole — it is written to be pasted, not edited — and drop it into one generator (Kling free credits, or Veo 3.1 if a spoken line matters). Expect 5–15 attempts before the framing is right.

Keep the take where the person reads as real and NO DEVICE SCREEN IS VISIBLE. Nothing else matters — not how pretty the bar is, not the colour grade. You can fix a grade in CapCut; you cannot fix an invented interface.

Recorded by you, at a desk. Phone for the three PR videos, iPad or browser for the agency and venue ones. Follow the video’s SCREEN RECORDING row tap by tap and its FRAME IT BIG row for what must stay legible.
This is the half that proves anything. The generated opener asks the question; only your recording answers it. Shoot each action three times and keep the calmest.
In CapCut: opener first, screen recording second, text on top. Export. Then WATCH IT ON YOUR PHONE and fix the worst thing. Export again. Repeat until nothing obvious is left — usually three passes.

The first output is a draft, never the post. Almost every fault found on pass one is the same three things: the proof is not held long enough, the text is too small, and the video starts before the hook.
CAPCUT — PHONE AND DESKTOP, AND WHY THEY ARE NOT THE SAME

PHONE app for the three PR videos — the footage is already on the phone, so nothing has to move. DESKTOP (capcut.com) for the agency and venue ones, where you are cutting iPad or browser recordings and want a bigger timeline for precise text timing.
Moving a 60 fps phone recording to a laptop and back loses a generation of quality for no reason.
Track 1 = the generated opener, trimmed to 1–2 s. Track 2 = your screen recording, butted straight against it. A hard cut, not a transition — no fades, no swipes, no zoom.
A transition between a generated shot and a real one draws attention to the join. A hard cut reads as one continuous thought.

Crop the recording to the panel that matters (Edit → Crop), then scale to fill the frame. Do this ONCE per shot as a fixed crop. If you need a closer view, that is a second clip with a tighter crop, cut in.
CapCut’s keyframed zoom is the exact camera drift the owner rejected. Crop, cut, never move.

Add a soft circle or a small glow at the click point at the moment of the tap — Stickers, or a shape with low opacity, 0.3 s. Enlarge the mouse cursor in system settings BEFORE recording the web ones.
A viewer who cannot see what was pressed assumes the result was typed in by hand.
Burn in the ON-SCREEN TEXT row at its stated timings. Big, high contrast, safe margin away from the edges, and never over the part of the screen the viewer is meant to read.
Most venue owners watch with the sound off. If the text does not carry the video alone, the video does not work.
One quiet music bed from CapCut’s free library, ducked under any voice. A single soft tick on the tap. Nothing else.
Pro-marked music adds a watermark, and a busy track makes a demo feel like an advert.
1080p, 30 fps, highest quality. Export EACH ratio separately by re-framing — 9:16 for Reels and 小红书, 4:5 for Facebook. Never letterbox one to fit the other.
A letterboxed Reel is read as a repost and gets buried.
ENHANCE, ENHANCE, ENHANCE — THE FIRST OUTPUT IS NEVER THE POST

Export, watch it on your own phone, fix the single worst thing, export again. Three passes is normal and four is fine for V4 and V8. Almost every fault on pass one is one of the same three: the proof is not held long enough, the text is too small, or the video starts before the hook.
Play it on your own phone at arm’s length, sound off. Can you read the one thing the FRAME IT BIG row names?
If you squint: crop tighter, or re-record at a higher browser zoom. This is the fault that wastes the most footage, and it is only visible on a phone — never on the laptop you edited on.
PASS 2 · Does it hold the proof?
Count the seconds the proof frame is on screen. Under one full second is too short.
The proof is the entire point. Everything else can lose time to it — the opener, the walk-in, the last beat.
PASS 3 · Does it start too early?
Watch the first 2 seconds alone. Is the question already there?
Cut everything before the hook. The commonest fault in a first output is three wasted seconds of setup.
PASS 4 · Would a stranger repeat it?
Show it to somebody who does not know InnocenZ and ask them what they just saw.
If they cannot say it back in one sentence, it is a feature clip, not an explanation — that is what the LONG cut is for.
When a pass produces no change worth exporting for. Usually three passes; four if it is V4 or V8.
Perfect never ships. Three passes and post it — the numbers will tell you more than a fourth pass would.
NO GREEN SCREEN — THE REAL SCREEN IS THE VIDEO

The old method put a generated phone in a generated bar and composited your screen onto a green rectangle. It is gone. Ask any video model for “a phone showing the InnocenZ payment screen” and it invents a convincing fake — wrong ringgit, invented tabs, a layout that is not yours — and it looks plausible enough that people believe it, which makes it worse than useless for a product demo.
What it means when you film
The screen recording IS the video
Not an ingredient, not a composite. You record the app doing the thing, and that footage is what gets posted. Free, and the only version that is true.
Every video lands on a PROOF

The state the app shows when the action worked — the distance stamp, the status chip changing, the evidence sheet open, the refusal. Hold on it for a full second. A video without that frame is an advert; with it, it is evidence.

No pan, no push-in, no drift left to right, no cutting to a second angle inside a shot. A locked frame reads as a recording; a moving one reads as a commercial, and people stop believing what is on the screen.
Keep the scene — lose the fake screen

The bar stool at closing time, the rain-damp doorway, the 2 a.m. desk: all of that stays, as a 1–2 second OPENING SHOT before the recording. It was never the problem and it is what stops a scroll. The only rule is that no device screen appears in it — film it yourself, or generate it with the phone face down or out of frame.
A model may make a cover graphic or an atmosphere shot with NO screen visible. That is the whole of its job now. It cannot invent an interface it is never asked to show.
Record before you plan the cut
The real footage sets the pacing and the length. Plan the edit around what you actually captured, not the other way round.
RECORD THE SCREEN PROPERLY — THE PART THAT COSTS NOTHING
iPhone: Screen Recording from Control Centre. Android: Screen record from quick settings. Record at the phone’s own resolution and never pinch-zoom while recording — zoom in the edit instead.
60 fps if the phone offers it, so a slowed slide-up stays smooth.

iPadOS: add Screen Recording to Control Centre, open the portal in Safari, hide the tab bar, then record. Hold the tablet in landscape so a 4:5 and a 16:9 crop both come out of the same take.

Fallback if the tablet will not cooperate: record the portal in a laptop browser at 100% zoom with the bookmarks bar hidden and one tab open, and never resize the window mid-take.
Agency owners and venue managers work off a tablet, so a tablet recording looks like their desk. A browser chrome full of tabs looks like a developer’s.
Do Not Disturb on. Notifications off. Battery above 50% so the icon is not red. Clock showing a believable hour for a nightlife shift.
A WhatsApp banner dropping into frame ruins an otherwise finished take.
A demo or test account with realistic-but-invented amounts. Never a real PR’s pay, IC, phone number or address — and demo names for the venue and agency too.
Consent covers a person’s face; it does not cover their pay.
Shoot every action three times and keep the calmest one. Move slower than feels natural — taps read as accidents at normal speed.
Give the proof frame a full second of stillness before you cut.
MAKE IT READABLE — RECORDING A PORTAL WITHOUT THE MESS

This section exists because a web portal does not survive being squeezed into a phone-shaped video. Do not record the page — record the PANEL, enlarged, with the click marked. Every video below names the one thing its viewer has to be able to read; if that thing is not legible at arm’s length on your own phone, the take is wasted no matter how true it is.
Zoom before you record, not after
Safari or the browser at 150–175% before the first take. The portals are built on a fixed type ladder, so they scale up cleanly rather than reflowing into a mess.
Zooming in the edit enlarges pixels. Zooming the browser enlarges the TEXT, and text is the only thing the viewer is trying to read.
Crop to the panel where the action happens. Sidebar, header, breadcrumbs and every other card are cropped out — not hidden later, framed out from the start.
A whole dashboard in a 4:5 frame is about 6 px of body text on a phone. Nobody reads it, so nothing is proved.
Enlarge the cursor in the system settings, pause half a second before and after every click, and add a soft pulse ring at the click point in the edit.
A viewer who cannot see what was clicked assumes the result was typed in by hand.
Full screen (F11), bookmarks bar off, one tab, no extensions visible, no notification badges.
Browser chrome dates the video, identifies your machine, and eats frame height you need for the product.
Play the take on your own phone, held normally. If you squint at the one thing the video exists to show, crop tighter and shoot again.
This is the only test that matters, and it takes ten seconds.
Need a closer look? That is a second shot with a tighter crop, cut in. Never a zoom or a pan inside a take.
Owner’s rule: one angle, start to end. A moving frame reads as an advert; a locked one reads as a recording.

STEP 3 · THE EDIT — WHERE THE TWO HALVES BECOME ONE SHOT

The obvious choice, phone or desktop
Everything this plan needs: multi-track timeline, chroma key (the green-screen composite the whole approach rests on), keyframes, speed ramping, burned-in captions, free music, 1080p export.

ORDER OF WORK — ONE VIDEO, START TO FINISH
